messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: sudden uptick in 5xx from serving-runtime-prod. Error signature: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (misaligned address). Affected nodes: gpu-7, gpu-12. Auto-fallback to CPU attempted for some routes. Rate: 4.6% over 30m. Paging oncall.

maya: I'm oncall. seeing repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` in runtime logs, containers OOM/exiting with code 139. This started ~10:12 UTC. Root traces:
```
Container runtime log: serving-runtime[pid=24321]: Assertion failed: illegal memory access at 0x7fffb2d16c00
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ... runtime::launch_kernel keras_kernel.cu:line 421
  CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```
And kernel dmesg: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=24321, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.1: couldn't move device to D0 state
[ 12346.000000] Backtrace: ...
```

maya: initial mitigation: scaled down batch size and applied model-routing fallback to cpu-variant for 60% of traffic. Still seeing container crashes on gpu-7.

andrea: quick Q - driver/kernel versions? any recent infra rollout?

lee: check `nvidia-smi` and kernel modules. If it's a misaligned address in CUDA kernels could be a model/kernel race when kv-cache allocation crosses page boundaries.

ryan: paging ops note: recommend cordon+drain affected nodes to force traffic away. we'll also enable a temporary rate limit on heavy routes.

maya: executing cordon/drain on gpu-7 now.
```
# commands run by oncall
kubectl cordon node/gpu-7
kubectl drain node/gpu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

ops-runner-bot: Autoscale policy triggered: provisioning 3 fallback-cpu pods in eu-west-1 to absorb traffic. :gear:

omar: I'll take traffic routing once nodes are drained. @maya paste the container logs from gpu-12 too.

maya: logs from gpu-12 attached (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z serving-runtime[pid=19877]: cuda runtime error: misaligned address on memcpy at 0x7fff2af87f20
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z serving-runtime[pid=19877]: stack: launch_kernel+0x3b4
2026-03-15T10:14:03Z containerd: process exited with status 139
```

andrea: not seeing infra driver rollout in last 72h fingerprint. Could be a new model variant using a custom CUDA op that exercises an alignment bug. Any recent model pushes?

maya: we did push quantized-merge-2 for redwood/gpt-small-quant ~8h ago. Rollback request in flight.

lee: mitigation checklist from runbook (short):
- cordon+drain node (done)
- route traffic to older model variants / cpu fallback (done)
- restart nvidia persistence daemon on node + collect `dmesg` (collecting)
- if crash persists, schedule node reboot and mark for hardware/driver inspection

maya: restarted `nvidia-persistenced` on gpu-7, checking `nvidia-smi` output.
```
$ sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
$ nvidia-smi
+------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id  Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40G   On         | 0000:65:00.0  | N/A                 |
+------------------------------------------------------+
```

maya: after restart we're still seeing one container crash then it stabilizes. Looks intermittent.

ops-runner-bot: executed autoscale fallback routing: 65% -> cpu-variant, 35% -> gpu pool (new routing rule id=rb-20260315-07).

omar: I'm taking over the incident. @maya please add any open customer tickets impacted. I'm going to coordinate a rolling reboot of gpu-12 and gpu-7 during low traffic window.

maya: customer-impact: internal metrics show 5 customers saw >10% error increase, public API route `/v1/generate` had 5xx spikes. Sent initial customer comms to #support.

lee: we should capture a repro and send to research for kernel-op debug. If it's a race in kernel kernels launching with shared buffers we need to add alignment checks in the custom op.

ryan: for live mitigation, suggestion: temporarily disable aggressive batching and prefetch path that touches large KV caches. That reduced memory churn for me in a similar event.

maya: applied `BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=1024` -> previous 4096. Error rate dropped to 0.9% in 15m window.

ops-runner-bot: Node reboot scheduled: gpu-12 @ 10:38 UTC (cordoned), gpu-7 @ 10:45 UTC. Draining confirmed.

maya: rebooted gpu-12. Post-reboot checks: `dmesg` cleared previous Xid messages. `nvidia-smi` healthy. No new crashes for 20m on rebooted node.

omar: after both reboots and CPU fallback routing, 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.2%. Rolling back temporary rate limits and keeping cpu-fallback at 30% for now.

andrea: opening post-incident ticket and assigning to `eng-runtime` and `research` for kernel-op root cause. We should capture: container core dumps, exact model commit, op kernels involved, driver version, and full dmesg.

maya: core dumps and kernel logs uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1918001234/ (internal link).

omar: handoff: I'm oncall for the next 6 hours. Owning follow-ups: postmortem, reproduce locally, and coordinate possible model rollback if reproduces. Marking incident P1 -> needs blameless postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Error rate returned to normal at 10:58 UTC. Final status: degraded -> mitigated.

maya: thanks team. please add any lingering action items to the ticket. I'll join the postmortem tomorrow.

ryan: action item: add alignment-safety checks to custom CUDA op and add a canary test with our quantized models in staging.

omar: noted. I'll assign owners and schedule dry-run of the canary next week.

ops-runner-bot: Closing run: autoscale rollback in 30m if no regressions.

maya: closing thread from oncall side, leaving handoff notes in ticket. Good job everyone. :tada:
